az_lieback_rock.blurb: Lieback Rock is a single prominent boulder beside the Back Porch, tucked into the Main Boulders zone of Groom Creek south of Prescott, at roughly 6,400 feet. A dozen problems cover a wide range: a few V0 warm-ups, a cluster around V2 and V3 that includes crack-flavoured lines, then a steady climb in difficulty through V4, V5 and V6 up to a couple of tough V7 and V8 testpieces. It suits a mixed group, since beginners and strong boulderers can both find something here. Because it sits within a larger field of boulders, plan to combine it with neighbouring blocks for a full session. Bring a pad or two and a spotter.

az_joel_s_house.blurb: Joel's House is a compact cluster of four big boulders in the Icecapades bouldering zone on the north side of Phoenix, at around 1,700 feet. Twelve problems spread over the blocks run from a gentle warm-up slab, through a handful of V0 to V3 lines, up to a V6 and a V8 for strong climbers. Expect textured but sharp stone, some long traverses, and landings that are workable rather than great, so a couple of pads and a spotter are worthwhile. The walk in follows desert trails shared with mountain bikers, and the setting is open desert, so summer heat makes the cooler months the sensible choice.

az_penguinland_area.blurb: Penguinland is the farthest-south sector of Raptor Ridge in Queen Creek Canyon, east of Phoenix at about 4,000 feet. It was passed over for years as too short and fragmented, but a closer look turned up a tidy group of crack climbs sitting side by side. All twelve routes are trad, from an easy 5.5 up to a 5.11 line, with most clustered around 5.10. Many were put up ground-up, so expect the occasional spicy placement. A shared two-bolt station on top of one of the cracks serves as the rappel point for several neighbouring lines. Bring a standard rack, with some wide pieces for the easier crack.
